method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reconstruction of both structural inductions, case-by-case replay of every primitive and defined connective branch, verification of assignment agreement at free variables and modified assignments at quantified variables, and exact projected formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Independence of term values and formula satisfaction from irrelevant variable assignments, sentence satisfaction, satisfaction of sentence sets, assignment-free semantics and Skolem normal form.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Although assignments give values to infinitely many variables, a term value depends only on variables occurring in the term, and formula satisfaction depends only on free variables of the formula. Agreement on those relevant variables therefore suffices.
samples.checks: The universal-assignment convenience, infinitely many variables, term/formula distinction, free-variable restriction and two precise agreement claims are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If two assignments agree on every variable of a term, the term has the same value under both. The proof handles constants and variables directly, then applies the induction hypothesis to each argument of a function term before applying the interpreted function.
samples.checks: Both base cases, the k subterms, every equality in the aligned calculation and the induction-hypothesis direction are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If two assignments agree on all free variables of a formula, satisfaction is invariant between them. The atomic base cases cover truth, falsity, predicates and identity; term-value invariance transfers each predicate argument and both sides of identity.
samples.checks: All atomic alternatives, the forward-direction convention and the symmetric reverse direction remain explicit. OLFOL-019 restores the predicate tuple's first index to t_1.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The induction step transfers satisfaction through negation and every binary connective. For existential and universal quantification, both assignments are modified to give x the same arbitrary domain value; they still agree away from x, so the induction hypothesis applies to the quantified body.
samples.checks: Each polarity and connective condition is retained. Both quantifier cases preserve domain scope, x-variant agreement, shared value m and the correct conclusion assignment. OLFOL-020 constructs the two universal variants from s_1 and s_2.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sentence has no free variables, so its satisfaction is independent of every assignment. A structure satisfies a sentence when it does so under all assignments, and satisfies a set Gamma when it satisfies every sentence in Gamma.
samples.checks: The proof-completion prompt, sentence corollary, assignment-free satisfaction notation, truth-in-a-structure wording and setwise universal condition are retained. OLFOL-021 removes only the duplicated Gamma.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Sentence satisfaction is equivalent to satisfaction under any fixed assignment. When A(x) has only x free, its existential closure is satisfied exactly when A holds under at least one assignment, and its universal closure exactly when A holds under every assignment.
samples.checks: Both proposition labels, proof exercises, quantifier tags and assignment quantifiers are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The first problem defines a satisfaction-style relation without variable assignments for a function-free language. Quantifiers are handled by reinterpreting a fresh constant at each domain element, and free variables are replaced by fresh constants interpreted at their assigned values.
samples.checks: The modified-structure notation, every recursive truth clause, freshness condition, complete free-variable/constant/domain-element lists and the target equivalence are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The final problem asks for the satisfiability equivalence between forall x exists y A(x,y) and its expansion by a new witness function f, forall x A(x,f(x)), identifying the latter as a Skolem normal form.
samples.checks: The freshness of f, existential claims about the two structures, both quantified formulas, theorem attribution and normal-form direction are preserved.

source_observations: OLFOL-019 changes the concluding predicate tuple's initial t_i to t_1.
OLFOL-020 constructs s_1-prime from s_1 and s_2-prime from s_2 in the universal induction case.
OLFOL-021 removes the second consecutive Gamma from the sentence-set definition.
After the three exact projections, all formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi x-variant and Skolem-normal-form headwords remain explicitly open to specialist review in T222 and T223.
Tag-dependent branches were reviewed from the source and proof semantics; no TeX reader build was run for this individual unit.
